answer_text:
Using periodicity and reduction formulas:

\[
\operatorname{tg}\left(\alpha-\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)
=\operatorname{tg}\left(\alpha+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)
=-\operatorname{ctg}\alpha
\]

and

\[
\operatorname{ctg}\left(\alpha+\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)
=\operatorname{ctg}\left(\alpha-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)
=-\operatorname{tg}\alpha.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\begin{aligned}
&\operatorname{tg}^{2}\left(\alpha-\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)
-\operatorname{ctg}^{2}\left(\alpha+\frac{3\pi}{2}\right) \\
&= (-\operatorname{ctg}\alpha)^2-(-\operatorname{tg}\alpha)^2 \\
&= \operatorname{ctg}^2\alpha-\operatorname{tg}^2\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\]

Now simplify further:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{ctg}^2\alpha-\operatorname{tg}^2\alpha
&= \frac{\cos^2\alpha}{\sin^2\alpha}-\frac{\sin^2\alpha}{\cos^2\alpha} \\
&= \frac{\cos^4\alpha-\sin^4\alpha}{\sin^2\alpha\cos^2\alpha} \\
&= \frac{(\cos^2\alpha-\sin^2\alpha)(\cos^2\alpha+\sin^2\alpha)}{\sin^2\alpha\cos^2\alpha} \\
&= \frac{\cos 2\alpha}{\sin^2\alpha\cos^2\alpha} \\
&= \frac{4\cos 2\alpha}{\sin^2 2\alpha}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus, for values where the original expression is defined,

\[
\boxed{\operatorname{ctg}^{2}\alpha-\operatorname{tg}^{2}\alpha
=\frac{4\cos 2\alpha}{\sin^2 2\alpha}}
\]
